arxiv-2201-03026.title: An Ensemble Approach to Acronym Extraction using Transformers
arxiv-2201-03026.creator: Prashant Sharma, Hadeel Saadany, Leonardo Zilio, Diptesh Kanojia, Constantin Orăsan
arxiv-2201-03026.description: Abstract Acronyms are abbreviated units of a phrase constructed by using initial components of the phrase in a text. Automatic extraction of acronyms from a text can help various Natural Language Processing tasks like machine translation, information retrieval, and text summarisation.

arxiv-2303-13279.title: Parameterized Algorithms for Topological Indices in Chemistry
arxiv-2303-13279.creator: Giovanna K. Conrado, Amir K. Goharshady, Harshit J. Motwani
arxiv-2303-13279.description: Abstract Abstract: We have developed efficient parameterized algorithms for the enumeration problems of graphs arising in chemistry. In particular, we have focused on the following problems: enumeration of Kekulé structures, computation of Hosoya index, computation of Merrifield–Simmons index, and computation of graph entropy based on matchings and independent sets. All these problems are known to be \#P -complete.

arxiv-2307-08622.title: Experimental Realization of Anti-Unitary Wave-Chaotic Photonic Topological Insulator Graphs Showing Kramers Degeneracy and Symplectic Ensemble Statistics
arxiv-2307-08622.creator: Shukai Ma, Steven M. Anlage
arxiv-2307-08622.description: Abstract Working in analogy with topological insulators in condensed matter, photonic topological insulators (PTI) have been experimentally realized, and protected electromagnetic edge-modes have been demonstrated in such systems. Moreover, PTI technology also emulates a synthetic spin-1/2 degree of freedom (DOF) in the reflectionless topological modes.

arxiv-2307-14465.title: What Kinds of Contracts Do ML APIs Need? Journal: Empirical Software Engineering
arxiv-2307-14465.creator: Samantha Syeda Khairunnesa, Shibbir Ahmed, Sayem Mohammad Imtiaz, Hridesh Rajan, Gary T. Leavens
arxiv-2307-14465.description: Abstract Recent work has shown that Machine Learning (ML) programs are error-prone and called for contracts for ML code. Contracts, as in the design by contract methodology, help document APIs and aid API users in writing correct code. The question is: what kinds of contracts would provide the most help to API users?

arxiv-2309-07522.title: A survey of complex generalized weighing matrices and a construction of quantum error-correcting codes
arxiv-2309-07522.creator: Ronan Egan
arxiv-2309-07522.description: Abstract Some combinatorial designs, such as Hadamard matrices, have been extensively researched and are familiar to readers across the spectrum of Science and Engineering. They arise in diverse fields such as cryptography, communication theory, and quantum computing. Objects like this also lend themselves to compelling mathematics problems, such as the Hadamard conjecture.

arxiv-2401-01181.title: Query-Based Knowledge Sharing for Open-Vocabulary Multi-Label Classification
arxiv-2401-01181.creator: Xuelin Zhu, Jian Liu, Dongqi Tang, Jiawei Ge, Weijia Liu, Bo Liu, Jiuxin Cao
arxiv-2401-01181.description: Abstract Identifying labels that did not appear during training, known as multi-label zero-shot learning, is a non-trivial task in computer vision. To this end, recent studies have attempted to explore the multi-modal knowledge of vision-language pre-training (VLP) models by knowledge distillation, allowing to recognize unseen labels in an open-vocabulary manner.

arxiv-2410-14545.creator: Frederic Kirstein, Terry Ruas, Robert Kratel, Bela Gipp

arxiv-2503-07658.title: There are more non-Cantorian sets than are Cantorian
arxiv-2503-07658.creator: Zuhair Al-Johar
arxiv-2503-07658.description: Abstract 1 Introduction When working in \sf NF , [1] there is a sense that there are more non-Cantorian sets than Cantorian sets. But it is not that immediate result as one expects, since they are externally equinumerous, and the qualification “Cantorian” is not stratified and so not easy to spell internally.

arxiv-2504-10688.title: Introducing Large Language Models as the Next Challenging Internet Traffic Source
arxiv-2504-10688.creator: Nataliia Koneva, Alejandro Leonardo García Navarro, Alfonso Sánchez-Macián, José Alberto Hernández, Moshe Zukerman, Óscar González de Dios
arxiv-2504-10688.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nataliia Koneva, Alejandro Leonardo García Navarro, Alfonso Sánchez-Macián, José Alberto Hernández, Moshe Zukerman, Óscar González de Dios. This article explores the growing impact of large language models (LLMs) and Generative AI (GenAI) tools on Internet traffic, focusing on their role as a new and significant source of network load. As these AI tools continue to gain importance in applications ranging from virtual assistants to content generation, the volume of traffic they generate is expected to increase massively.

arxiv-2510-16227.title: What Can String Probability Tell Us About Grammaticality?
arxiv-2510-16227.creator: Jennifer Hu, Ethan Gotlieb Wilcox, Siyuan Song, Kyle Mahowald, Roger P. Levy
arxiv-2510-16227.description: Abstract What have language models (LMs) learned about grammar? This question remains hotly debated, with major ramifications for linguistic theory. However, since probability and grammaticality are distinct notions in linguistics, it is not obvious what string probabilities can reveal about an LM’s underlying grammatical knowledge.

arxiv-2511-08056.title: Realization of an all-optical effective negative-mass oscillator for coherent quantum noise cancellation
arxiv-2511-08056.creator: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, Michèle Heurs
arxiv-2511-08056.description: Abstract We report the realization of an all-optical, tabletop effective-negative-mass oscillator (ENMO) scheme capable of canceling quantum noise when cascaded with an opto-mechanical sensor susceptible to (quantum) radiation pressure noise. Our coherent quantum noise cancellation (CQNC) scheme offers a broadband cancellation capability with a tunable, wavelength-flexible, and compact system.

pmc-10751346.title: The genetic puzzle of a SOD1-patient with ocular ptosis and a motor neuron disease: a case report
pmc-10751346.creator: Veria Vacchiano, Flavia Palombo, Danara Ormanbekova, Claudio Fiorini, Alessia Fiorentino, Leonardo Caporali, Andrea Mastrangelo, Maria Lucia Valentino, Sabina Capellari, Rocco Liguori, Valerio Carelli
pmc-10751346.description: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a neurodegenerative disease with a complex genetic architecture, showing monogenic, oligogenic, and polygenic inheritance. In this study, we describe the case of a 71 years-old man diagnosed with ALS with atypical clinical features consisting in progressive ocular ptosis and sensorineural deafness.

pmc-11394296.title: A Narrative Review: Repurposing Metformin as a Potential Therapeutic Agent for Oral Cancer
pmc-11394296.creator: Jui-Hsiang Li, Pei-Yi Hsin, Yung-Chia Hsiao, Bo-Jun Chen, Zhi-Yun Zhuang, Chiang-Wen Lee, Wei-Ju Lee, Thi Thuy Tien Vo, Chien-Fu Tseng, Shih-Fen Tseng, I-Ta Lee
pmc-11394296.description: Simple SummaryOral cancer, particularly oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), is a widespread health problem with limited treatment options and poor survival rates. Metformin, a common medication for managing diabetes, has recently shown promise as a potential treatment for various cancers, including OSCC. This review examines the potential benefits of repurposing metformin to treat oral cancer.

pmc-11511518.title: Simultaneous Degradation of AFB1 and ZEN by CotA Laccase from Bacillus subtilis ZJ-2019-1 in the Mediator-Assisted or Immobilization System
pmc-11511518.creator: Boquan Gao, Wei An, Jianwen Wu, Xiumin Wang, Bing Han, Hui Tao, Jie Liu, Zhenlong Wang, Jinquan Wang
pmc-11511518.description: The global prevalence of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) and zearalenone (ZEN) contamination in food and feed poses a serious health risk to humans and animals. Recently, enzymatic detoxification has received increasing attention, yet most enzymes are limited to degrading only one type of mycotoxin, and free enzymes often exhibit reduced stability and activity, limiting their practicality in real-world applications.

pmc-12411789.title: Hemodynamic Assessment of Arterial Perfusion by Using the Ultrasonographic Hand Acceleration Time: Protocol for a Cross-Sectional Prospective Descriptive Study
pmc-12411789.creator: Begoña Gonzalo, Sebastián Videla, José Moranas, Thiago Carnaval, Carolina Herranz, Emma Espinar, Elena Iborra
pmc-12411789.description: BackgroundSeveral noninvasive methods can be used to assess hand perfusion, but none have been standardized for diagnosing chronic upper limb ischemia. One potentially useful diagnostic tool for this purpose is the ultrasonographic hand acceleration time (HAT), although it still requires characterization and validation.

pmc-12566285.title: Deciphering the Impact of Mutations on PfDHPS Active Site and Sulfadoxine Binding: Structural Insights from Molecular Dynamics Simulations
pmc-12566285.creator: Emilie Guémas, Sandie Ménard, Nicolas Jeanne, Georges Landa, Antoine Berry, Marie Brut, Anna Maria Almerico
pmc-12566285.description: The antimalarial combination of sulfadoxine–pyrimethamine is used as a preventive treatment in pregnant women and children in Africa. Sulfadoxine inhibits the Plasmodium falciparum dihydropteroate synthase (PfDHPS), but resistance has emerged through point mutations in this enzyme. In this study, we investigate the impact of mutations on the structural and dynamic properties of PfDHPS using molecular dynamics simulations.

pmc-12811976.title: Efavirenz-Induced Hepatitis Mimicking Autoimmune Hepatitis: A Case Report
pmc-12811976.creator: Adibul H Chowdhury, Dristy Chowdhury, Israt Jahan, Adaze Woghiren, Mohamed Saleh
pmc-12811976.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Efavirenz is a widely used and effective non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) for the treatment of HIV. Hepatotoxicity, although recognized, typically occurs early in the course of NNRTI therapy. However, delayed liver injury resembling autoimmune hepatitis is rare. We report a 62-year-old HIV-positive man on long-term efavirenz who developed new, asymptomatic elevations in liver enzymes after years of stable antiretroviral therapy. Work-up revealed elevated levels antinuclear antibodies (ANA) IgG after exclusion of metabolic and viral hepatitis.

pmc-13058729.title: Antibacterial prophylaxis and antimicrobial stewardship in the era of innovative therapies for haematological malignancies: transplantation, cellular therapies and new drugs
pmc-13058729.creator: R Dell’Acqua, M H Parrinello, D Clerici, F Farina, V Spagnuolo, M Ranzenigo, M Negri, R Greco, C Corti, A Castagna, F Ciceri, M Ripa
pmc-13058729.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Antibacterial prophylaxis has long been a cornerstone of supportive care in patients with haematological malignancies undergoing intensive chemotherapy and haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), particularly in the setting of prolonged and profound neutropenia. However, the widespread use of fluoroquinolone (FQ) prophylaxis has increasingly raised concerns related to antimicrobial resistance, microbiota disruption, drug-related toxicity, and Clostridioides difficile infection, challenging its universal application.

pmc-13380215.title: Small proline-rich repeat protein 1A-mediated ephrin-A5 downregulation drives neuropathic pain via brain-derived neurotrophic factor/Tropomyosin receptor kinase B signaling
pmc-13380215.creator: Meiling Deng, Ting Zhang, Jie Yang, Qiqi Yan, Jun Yang, Wangyuan Zou, Jun Cao, Li Ren
pmc-13380215.description: Neuropathic pain is a common chronic pain condition that severely impacts patients’ quality of life. While Small proline-rich protein 1A (SPRR1A) is a well-known marker for axonal regeneration, its specific role and the underlying molecular mechanisms in neuropathic pain remain elusive.

pmc-13631256.title: Considering microRNAs as measures of extrinsic domains of risk in the context of underlying genetic characteristics: type 2 diabetes as an exemplar
pmc-13631256.creator: Benjamin M. Stroebel, Alexis Jimenez, Karla J. Lindquist, Dara Torgerson, Kayla D. Longoria, J. Cesar Ignacio-Espinoza, Elena Flowers
pmc-13631256.description: The etiology of most health conditions is complex, arising from a combination of risk factors that include both intrinsic (i.e., genetic characteristics) and extrinsic (e.g., behaviors, the environment, social factors) domains. Until relatively recently, health science research typically conflated the biological construct of genetic ancestry with the social constructs of race and ethnicity.
